Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of acts of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 68

The Family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in: a. protecting women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;

b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and

c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring: a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social lives; and b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life. (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PADANG PARIAMAN,

CHAPTER III

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for Children who are victims of acts of Violence.

Article 46

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing his/her personality and level of intelligence in accordance with interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to obtain Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents must endeavor to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 45

(1) Every education unit organizer is obliged to provide opportunities for Children to obtain education services without discrimination.

(2) Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of acts of Violence drops out of school, the education unit organizer must coordinate with the relevant agencies.

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents must endeavor to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of acts of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring: a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social lives; and b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life. (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 66

(1) The participation of the community in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;

Article 68

The Family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in: a. protecting women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;

b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and

c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

Article 25

Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents must endeavor to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

(1) Every education unit organizer is obliged to provide opportunities for Children to obtain education services without discrimination.

(2) Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of acts of Violence drops out of school, the education unit organizer must coordinate with the relevant agencies.

Community Organization is an organization founded and formed by the community voluntarily based on shared aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and objectives to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents must endeavor to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and local wisdom values of the local community.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Effectiveness of Services for Women Victims of Acts of Violence

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of acts of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring: a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social lives; and b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life. (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 31

Regional Governments implement repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(1) Repatriation is aimed at returning women victims of acts of Violence to their Region of origin.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 40

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 39 letter a constitute communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in the population and family planning Program.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring: a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social lives; and b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life. (3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 40

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 39 letter a constitute communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in the population and family planning Program.

Article 68

The Family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in: a. protecting women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;

b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and

c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 66

(1) The participation of the community in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;

c. monitors the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and local wisdom values of the local community.

Article 34

(1) In order to improve family quality, Regional Governments are responsible for:

a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and the rights of Children;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and the rights of Children.
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in the Region; and
(2) The responsibility of Regional Governments in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by SKPD in accordance with its duties and functions.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF PADANG PARIAMAN REGENCY and

HAS DECIDED:

To stipulate: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of acts of Violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 25

(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential. (4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:

a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of: a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 59

(1) In implementing the fulfillment of Children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regional Government facilitates the establishment of the Child Forum.

5.4.text:
Article 46

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing his/her personality and level of intelligence in accordance with interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to obtain Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 45

(1) Every education unit organizer is obliged to provide opportunities for Children to obtain education services without discrimination.

(2) Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of acts of Violence drops out of school, the education unit organizer must coordinate with the relevant agencies.

Article 63

In carrying out its duties, the KLA Task Force may coordinate and cooperate with PPT institutions and other institutions that provide Child Protection services.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 48

(1) Regional Governments are obliged to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains an optimal level of health from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents must endeavor to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for Children who are victims of acts of Violence.

CHAPTER VII

CHILD PROTECTION

Article 23

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services: a. counseling;

b. provision of safe houses; and

c. spiritual guidance.

(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:

a. SKPD having duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing community organizations in the social field; or
c. ministry of religious affairs.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by the Regional Government Supervisory Agency of Padang Pariaman Regency and P2TP2A;

(2) In carrying out supervision, P2TP2A is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law

(3) Recommendations submitted by P2TP2A must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

Article 66

(1) The participation of the community in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participates in prevention and provides support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;
b. provides information and/or reports violations of the rights of women and Children to the authorities; and
c. monitors the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

Article 59

(1) In implementing the fulfillment of Children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regional Government facilitates the establishment of the Child Forum.

(2) The Child Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) is a representation of Children in the Region, both representation of Children's geographical domicile, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.

(3) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regional Government must pay attention to and accommodate the opinions of Children submitted through the Child participation Forum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Child Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Rumah Aman etc.)
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints: a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedure for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to protect, strengthen human rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not yet married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a platform for Children's participation established with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the approval and willingness of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with their age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions resulting in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threats of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental well-being through the strengthening of the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relation gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every institution of state organizer, corporation, independent institution established based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities established solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 68

The Family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in: a. protecting women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;

b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and

c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 32

(1) Employers who employ women must maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.

(2) Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.

(3) Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations. (4) Employers must provide special breastfeeding facilities at their companies.

Article 33

(1) Female workers/laborers who are under 18 (eighteen) years of age are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB.
